objections.q: Why pay an ongoing fee when I rarely trade?
objections.a: The fee pays for ongoing advice, portfolio construction to the CIO's allocation, monitoring and rebalancing, and tax management, not for trades. If you truly want to buy and hold with little advice, a commission account can cost less, and we will show you both.

objections.q: Do I have to sell everything to move?
objections.a: No. Most positions can move as they are. Appreciated holdings are sold over time within a yearly gain budget, and some may stay where they are.

objections.q: My portfolio has done well. Why change it?
objections.a: Past returns came with more risk than your profile calls for. The proposal aims for similar expected return with less risk, and a plan if markets fall.

objections.q: I don't want to give up my company stock.
objections.a: You don't have to sell it all. We can reduce it in steps that fit your tax position, protect part of it, or give some away, and we follow any trading rules that apply to you.

objections.q: Is now a bad time to invest my cash?
objections.a: Nobody can time markets reliably. Investing in steps over several months spreads the entry point; it reduces regret, not long-run risk.

objections.q: Isn't a cheaper index-only option enough?
objections.a: It may be. The index-only portfolio costs less but has fewer services and no custom tax management. We will show both, and how advisor compensation differs.
